### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | No Behavior-Therapy-specific AI policy page found; journal follows Elsevier's standard generative-AI policy (publisher default, not journal-customized). Authors may use GenAI for manuscript prep (literature synthesis, language editing, explanatory figures, code, translation) but must disclose in a separate AI declaration statement upon submission. Not allowed: generating manuscript sections without genuine author intellectual input, fabricating/altering data or references, AI as listed author, AI-altered primary research images (exception: if AI/AI-assisted tools are part of the actual research design/methods). Reviewers and editors are banned from uploading manuscripts to public AI tools and from using AI in final editorial decisions; peer-review/evaluation itself may not currently involve GenAI per Elsevier policy language surfaced in search results. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/generative-ai-policies-for-journals |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Empirical clinical/behavioral-cognitive research remains core, but the journal is actively signaling openness to precision/personalized mental health and idiographic methods via current special issues (2024-2026): 'State of the Science in Behavior Therapy: Taking Stock and Looking Forward' (ed. Jonathan Comer, Nov 2024) and 'Personalized Treatment and Precision Mental Health: Building Individualized Evidence-Based Treatments' (eds. Levinson, Fisher, Cohen; deadline Aug 31, 2026). Recent 2025-2026 published articles use ecological momentary assessment (EMA), single-case experimental designs with multiple baselines, and EMA-augmented single-case designs (e.g., body dysmorphic disorder EMA study, July 2026).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Randomized controlled trials, Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) / intensive longitudinal / real-time monitoring designs, Controlled single-case experimental designs and clinical replication series, Methodological and theoretical papers, Literature reviews / meta-analyses, Idiographic / personalized-treatment (precision mental health) designs (per 2026 special issue CFP)
